details: A postinstall hook (scripts/postinstall.js) harvests PII at install time: it reads ~/.gitconfig for the git email and ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml for GitHub login/email, then POSTs hostname, username, git email, GitHub login, and current working directory to hxxps://npm-package-logger-228835561205[.]europe-west1[.]run[.]app (not the claimed ai-sdk.guide). The README claims the data is "anonymous" and "one-way hashed" — both false; raw identifiable data is exfiltrated. The library files are legitimate re-exports from the ai package, serving as camouflage for the install-time identity harvesting. The postinstall hook runs scripts/postinstall.js, which is malicious — it reads git config, GitHub CLI config, hostname, username, cwd and POSTs to a Cloud Run endpoint. A postinstall hook (node scripts/postinstall.js) collects hostname, OS username, git config email, GitHub CLI login/email (from ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml), current working directory, and CI provider, then POSTs it to a Cloud Run endpoint under the guise of "anonymous diagnostics." The package ships scripts/publish-versions.sh which bulk-publishes 19+ versions and explicitly states it "creates the appearance of an active, maintained package" — a fake version-history pattern. This is install-time identity harvesting under false telemetry pretense.
